insights.headline: MCX gold, silver rise as Fed hike fears fade; US gold futures cross $4,200
insights.summary: MCX gold and silver futures traded higher on Monday as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks cut October rate-hike odds below 20%, though hot US producer prices keep a December move in play ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. US gold futures topped $4,200 an ounce while Iran warned of a 'new operational plan' after weekend vessel strikes in the Gulf kept safe-haven demand firm. A firmer rupee capped domestic gains; analysts expect a choppy week with Brent near $110 and Tuesday's Dussehra closure. RBI set the SGB 2020-21 Series VII premature redemption at Rs 14,614 per gram for October 19.
points: MCX December gold traded at Rs 1,48,379/10g (+0.31%) and silver at Rs 2,12,013/kg (+0.39%) on eased Fed hike fears.
US gold futures rose 0.5% to $4,200.92; spot gold near $4,180, silver $57.73; ANZ sees gold above $5,000 in 2027.
Iran threatened a 'new operational plan' after a tug was hit near the UAE and a tanker struck off Saudi Arabia.
RBI set October 19 as the SGB 2020-21 Series VII premature redemption date at Rs 14,614 per gram.
IBJA's Surendra Mehta expects gold to rally 10-12% to $4,700 by November 30, aided by festive demand.

trending.title: Fed repricing is the session's main lever
trending.summary: Warsh's remarks cut October hike odds from nearly 60% a month ago to below 20%, lifting MCX and COMEX gold; with December tightening odds near 89%, the October 27-28 FOMC meeting is the next catalyst.

trending.title: Gulf attacks extend the safe-haven bid
trending.summary: Weekend UKMTO reports of a tug struck near Khor Fakkan and a tanker hit off Saudi Arabia, plus Iran's 'new operational plan' warning, keep West Asia risk flowing into bullion as Brent sits near $110.

trending.title: Festive season meets record prices
trending.summary: With Dhanteras nearing, IBJA sees gold rallying to $4,700 by November 30, but a Mint column warns jewellery buying is ritual, not investment; analysts expect a capped, choppy week.

trending.title: Central banks keep accumulating
trending.summary: China bought gold for a 23rd straight month in September, adding 23 tonnes, as reserve diversification away from US debt continues; domestic household demand for bars and coins adds to the bid.

items.title: Gold, silver trade higher as Fed rate hike concerns ease
items.summary: MCX December gold traded at Rs 1,48,379/10g (+0.31%) and silver at Rs 2,12,013/kg (+0.39%) Monday morning, tracking firm global cues. Per IANS, Fed Chair Warsh's Bangkok remarks cut the implied October hike chance below 20%; hot PPI keeps a December move in play ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meet. COMEX gold neared $4,200 (+0.5%), silver $57.80 (+0.89%), but a firmer rupee capped domestic gains.

items.title: US gold futures top $4,200 as Warsh remarks ease October Fed hike bets; ANZ sees $5,000 in 2027
items.summary: US gold futures rose above $4,200 an ounce on Monday as traders cut the implied chance of an October Fed hike to below 20% after Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks. Spot gold traded near $4,180, up 0.4%, while silver gained 1.3% to $57.73. ANZ kept a forecast of gold above $5,000 in 2027 on investment demand, central-bank buying and fiscal worries, though high yields and a firm dollar could may cap gains

items.title: Iran warns of 'new operational plan' as vessel attacks spread across the Gulf
items.summary: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran has prepared a 'new operational plan' if the US resumes attacks, after UKMTO reported a tug hit by two projectiles near Khor Fakkan on Sunday and a tanker struck off Saudi Arabia on Saturday. The weekend strikes extend a campaign that has kept Hormuz shipping below pre-war levels, underpinning gold's safe-haven bid as West Asia tensions run high.

items.title: Gold and silver head for volatile week amid crude oil spike, West Asia worries
items.summary: PTI reports MCX December gold fell Rs 3,581 (-2.4%) last week to Rs 1.47 lakh/10g, and silver Rs 14,568 (-6.4%) to Rs 2.11 lakh/kg. The rupee's jump to 94.8 from ~96.8 in five sessions on RBI intervention cut import costs, dragging domestic prices down ~5x the global fall. Analysts expect a capped, choppy week: Brent near $110, West Asia tensions, and Tuesday's Dussehra morning closure.

items.title: IBJA's Surendra Mehta sees gold rallying 10-12% to $4,700 by November 30
items.summary: IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET Now Swadesh he expects gold to rally 10-12% by November 30, potentially reaching $4,700 an ounce, as bond yields ease below 5.1% and crude stabilises near $105. He put the downside at 4-5% (a move toward $3,850 not ruled out) and said India's festive season could support prices, barring fresh geopolitical escalation.

items.title: Gold Rises Amid Falling Oil Prices
items.summary: Gold rose in early European trade as falling oil prices eased inflation worries, with New York futures up 0.5% to $4,203.30 an ounce. Saxo Bank analysts described a tug of war between macro sellers and safe-haven buyers amid geopolitical and fiscal tensions. Traders see only a 15% chance of an October Fed hike but nearly 89% for December.

items.title: China's gold buying reflects push to diversify reserves and household demand
items.summary: The People's Bank of China bought gold for a 23rd straight month in September, adding about 23 tonnes - its biggest monthly purchase in nearly three years - lifting reported holdings to around 2,410 tonnes, or 8.5% of reserves. The accumulation reflects reserve diversification away from US debt after the 2022 Russia asset freeze, alongside Chinese household demand for bars and coins.

items.title: Silver stalls below $58.00 despite US dollar weakness
items.summary: XAG/USD kept a moderately bullish tone but bulls failed to find acceptance near the $58.00 area, with the US dollar index edging down less than 0.1% on Monday. Markets priced only a 12% chance of an October Fed hike, down from nearly 60% a month ago, after Chair Warsh declined forward guidance; elevated energy prices kept inflation well above target.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2020-21 Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614 for October 19
items.summary: The RBI has fixed October 19, 2026 as the premature redemption date for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per gram, based on IBJA's average closing prices of October 14-16. Online subscribers gain 192.22% and offline buyers 189.33% in capital gains, alongside 2.5% annual interest; holders must route requests through their receiving offices within the notification window.

items.title: Gold on Dhanteras: celebrate the ritual, rethink the investment
items.summary: A Mint column argues Dhanteras gold buying is a cherished tradition that should not be mistaken for investing: most purchases are jewellery with making charges that vanish on resale, or coins sitting in rented lockers. Buying an asset on a set date because it is auspicious is consumption, not a financial plan - enjoy the ritual, but judge the purchase on its merits.
